meta.description: Generates complete dual-disease transcriptomic + machine learning research designs from a user-provided disease pair. Use when users want to identify shared DEGs, common hub genes, cross-disease biomarkers, or shared molecular mechanisms between two diseases using public GEO data. Triggers: 'shared biomarker study for two diseases', 'dual-disease transcriptomic ML paper', 'identify common DEGs between disease A and B', 'cross-disease hub gene discovery', 'shared DEG + PPI + ROC design', 'immune infiltration shared biomarker', or 'I want to study disease X and Y together'. Always outputs four workload configurations (Lite / Standard / Advanced / Publication+) with a recommended primary plan, step-by-step workflow, figure plan, validation strategy, minimal executable version, and publication upgrade path.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID numbers, clinical trial results, sample sizes, p-values, or efficacy data. All GEO references are clearly labeled as examples (GSE48350, GSE7621). All statistical thresholds are field-standard (logFC > 1, adj.p < 0.05, AUC > 0.70, STRING confidence > 0.4).

practice_boundaries.detail: No direct diagnostic or prescriptive medical conclusions. Skill generates research protocols for comparative transcriptomic analysis, not clinical decisions. Proper disclaimers included (GEO data de-identified, no IRB required). No unapproved treatment recommendations.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacies. Ethical compliance clearly stated (GEO data = de-identified, no IRB required). Tissue compatibility issues explicitly addressed with resolution strategies (T2D/NAFLD liver tissue, COVID-19 data availability warnings). Validation strategies are methodologically sound (discovery + validation cohorts, cross-platform reproducibility, bootstrap CI).

code_usability.detail: No code generated. Mode A execution (direct instruction following). Skill references standard bioinformatics tools (limma, clusterProfiler, STRING, CytoHubba, CIBERSORT) but does not generate runnable code.

functional_suitability.note: Complete coverage of dual-disease transcriptomic research design: DEG identification, PPI analysis, hub gene discovery, ROC validation, immune infiltration, figure planning, and 4 workload tiers. Methods are scientifically sound using established tools.

reliability.note: Excellent fault tolerance with explicit zero-DEG recovery logic (relax threshold → top-500 → WGCNA), tissue-tool mismatch handling, and data availability warnings. Clear error reporting for impossible scenarios.

performance_context.note: Comprehensive output (~3-5k tokens typical) well-structured and necessary for research planning. Reference files reduce redundancy. Minor deduction for token cost.

agent_usability.note: Excellent learnability with clear trigger phrases and comprehensive when-to-use section. Consistent 9-step output format with uniform terminology. Each step includes rationale and field-standard justifications. Strong error prevention with input validation and escape hatches.

human_usability.note: Excellent discoverability with comprehensive description and multiple trigger examples. Forgiving design offers alternatives when pairing is inappropriate and provides upgrade paths.

security.note: No credentials required, uses only public GEO data. Strong input validation for disease appropriateness and tissue compatibility. No PHI handling.

maintainability.note: Excellent modularity with well-separated reference files (tissue_and_tool_decisions.md, geo_search_and_tools.md, figure_plan_template.md, upgrade_path.md). Easy to update thresholds, tools, or add new disease classes. Clear expected outputs enable testability.

agent_specific.note: Multiple precise trigger examples provided. Excellent progressive disclosure via 4 workload tiers. High composability with literature search and statistical analysis skills. Idempotent design produces consistent plan structure. Good escape hatch for out-of-scope requests. Minor deduction: could be more explicit about single-disease alternatives.

key_strengths: Comprehensive 9-step workflow structure covering all aspects of dual-disease transcriptomic research design (tissue selection, DEG analysis, PPI networks, hub genes, ROC validation, immune infiltration, figure planning, validation strategy, upgrade paths)

Excellent reference file system with 4 specialized reference files providing tissue-tool decisions, GEO search strategies, figure templates, and upgrade paths that reduce redundancy and improve maintainability
Strong fault tolerance with explicit zero-DEG recovery logic (relax threshold → top-500 → WGCNA), tissue mismatch handling, and data availability warnings for edge cases
Progressive disclosure via 4 workload tiers (Lite/Standard/Advanced/Publication+) with clear effort estimates (2-3 weeks to 12-16 weeks) and upgrade paths addressing specific reviewer concerns

Robust scope boundary and input validation correctly identifying and redirecting out-of-scope requests (3-disease comparison) and invalid inputs (non-disease comparators) with helpful alternative suggestions

recommendations.title: Enhance cross-platform validation guidance
recommendations.problem: Cross-platform validation (microarray → RNA-seq) is mentioned in Publication+ tier but detailed guidance on platform-specific normalization differences and batch correction strategies is not provided in reference files
recommendations.root_cause: Reference files focus on tool selection (GPL platforms, CytoHubba algorithms) but not cross-platform harmonization best practices
recommendations.fix: Add section to geo_search_and_tools.md titled 'Cross-Platform Comparison Best Practices' covering: (1) Microarray-to-RNA-seq normalization differences (RMA/MAS5 vs TPM/FPKM), (2) Batch effect correction strategies (ComBat for cross-platform), (3) Gene ID mapping (probe ID to gene symbol), (4) Expected concordance thresholds (≥80% for hub genes)

recommendations.title: Add explicit single-disease alternative in escape hatch
recommendations.problem: When user provides one disease + invalid comparator (e.g., depression vs happiness), skill redirects to alternative dual-disease pairings but does not explicitly point to single-disease analysis skills or standard DEG workflows
recommendations.root_cause: Escape hatch section focuses on dual-disease alternatives (other valid disease pairs) but not single-disease alternatives
recommendations.fix: Add to 'When NOT to Use' section: 'For single-disease analysis (one disease vs healthy controls), this skill is not appropriate. Use a single-disease transcriptomic analysis skill or conduct standard DEG analysis workflow (disease vs control, no cross-disease comparison).'
